tasks.title: Location A - Maynooth University - Features and aspects of wellness
tasks.statement: Walk around the campuses of Maynooth University. Create 6-8 categories that represent the wellness features that can be found on the North and South campuses of the university. Count the number of the features you see. Record these in table A1. Some features may be in more than one category.

parts.question: Look around both campuses of Maynooth University. Name an example of a wellness feature for each category, in table A1.
parts.reference: Give 4 marks if 8+ features are named in total. Give 3 marks if 6+ are named in total. Give 2 marks if 4+ are named in total. Give 1 marks if 2+ are named in total.

parts.question: Give two differences between the provision of wellness features on the North and South Campuses. For each difference, explain why this might be the case.
parts.reference: 1 mark for each difference named, with 2 marks for each reason given. (1 named difference + 2 reasons x 2 = 6 marks).

parts.question: Chose one wellness feature that you have identified. Describe how it would improve 3 aspects of wellness.
parts.reference: 1 marks for each aspect named, with 1 marks for each reason why it would improve wellness (1 aspect plus 1 improvement x 3 = 6 marks).

parts.question: Think of an additional element that could be added to promote wellness in at least two aspects on the North or South campus of the university. Draw a sketch of your feature as it might look when constructed. Annotate the sketch to describe key aspects of your feature.
parts.reference: 1 mark for an appropriate sketch. 1 mark for each key element / aspect of the feature described in the annotations, to the maximum of 3 marks (1 for sketch, up to 3 for element annotations = 4 marks).

tasks.title: Location B – Main Street – People and place
tasks.statement: Observe the street. Notice how people use the street pavement and roads, e.g. walking, scooting, cycling or driving.

parts.question: Look around and decide, how easy or challenging you think it is to do every day activities on Main St. Record your ideas with a tick. What do you notice from completing the table above? Describe two observations.
parts.reference: Credit 2 marks for completing the data collection table. Credit 1 mark per observation (2 for table, and 2 x 1 mark for observations = 4 marks).

parts.question: On the map below focus on the area of Main Street (Leinster Street). Label 4 points on the map below to show where there are 2 features that cause accessibility problems and 2 features that make the street accessible. Ensure you add a sentence to each of the 4, to say why they cause problems or help with accessibility.
parts.reference: 4 x 2 marks for feature being marked, labelled and a reason why it causes problems being noted (4 features names x 1 mark + 4 descriptions x 1 mark = 8 marks).

parts.question: Complete the table below to explain two ways in which you would change the street to make it more accessible for people.
parts.reference: 2 marks for description of change x 2 + 2 marks for difficulties = 8 marks.

tasks.title: Location C - Maynooth Train Station
tasks.statement: Find a safe position where you can see Maynooth Train Station.

parts.question: Draw a field sketch of Maynooth Train Station, label with the different categories of buildings, roads, footpaths and bridges, access points, and any other geographical features.
parts.reference: 1 mark for each feature marked, using words with arrow type labels or the use of a key = 6 marks.

parts.question: Complete the matrix below to compare the accessibility of different parts of the station for different groups of people. Score each place out of 5.
parts.reference: 4 marks for completed table. 3 marks for completed, with some ambiguity. 2 marks if ticked only. 1 mark if partly completed.

parts.question: Create a land use map of the locality of Maynooth station using the base map below. Decide on suitable categories and how to represent them. Label your map with a title and create a suitable legend / key.
parts.reference: Land use categories, 1 mark for each 1 to a max of 2 marks. Accurately positioned 4 marks. Labelled or included in key 4 marks (2 marks for 4 land uses, 4 marks for positioning / locations + 4 marks for use of key / labels = 10 marks).

tasks.title: Activity PSA-1 People in Maynooth
tasks.statement: Review the population pyramid and train passenger statistics for Maynooth.

parts.question: Describe two features of the population living in Maynooth that you observe in the population pyramid in diagram PSA-1.
parts.reference: 1 mark for each feature noted (1 feature x 1 = 2 marks).

parts.question: In the space below, construct a graph to give a visual presentation of the data in the table above. Give your graph a title and label it appropriately.
parts.reference: 1 mark for appropriate type of graph – bar. 1 mark for title and labelling. (1 accurate graph + titles and labelled = 6 marks, plus 2 marks from the table data representation part).

tasks.title: Activity PSA-2 Expanding passenger numbers
tasks.statement: Re-read the article on the expansion of the railway (Source 4). Think about the expansion of the railway services and the increase in passengers using the station.

parts.question: Describe 2 advantages the expansion of railway passenger numbers will bring to the area of Maynooth near the station.
Describe 2 disadvantages the expansion of railway passenger numbers will bring to the area of Maynooth near the station?

tasks.title: Activity PSA-3 Problems at the station
tasks.statement: You have been asked by Kildare County Council to produce resources and ideas to support an Active Travel Plan for the area around Maynooth Station for when the passenger numbers increase.

parts.question: On the aerial photograph below, annotate the photo to name and explain 4 problems at the station.
parts.reference: 1 mark for each problem named and annotated. 1 mark for explanation of why it is a problem as an annotation (4 problems: 1 mark for a name & annotation + 1 mark for explanation = 8 marks).

tasks.title: Activity PSA-4 Creating a Station plan
tasks.statement: Use your geographical knowledge, observations and skills to make a map of a more accessible Maynooth Station.

parts.question: Annotate your map to justify the features you have included.
parts.reference: 1 mark for title. 1 mark for use of key. 1 mark for each feature of the station, e.g. new bridge, improved footpaths, ramps, planting, etc. 2 marks for the justification of each feature. 4 features and their justification = 12. Up to 4 marks for naming features only.

tasks.title: Activity PSA-5 Opportunities and risks
tasks.statement: Think about the long-term sustainability of your proposed plan.

parts.question: Describe 3 possible benefits and 3 risks for your plan in each of the aspects in the table (Environmental, Financial, Social).
parts.reference: 1 mark for each benefit, 1 mark for each risk (3 benefits and 3 risks = 6 marks).
